$comment: Initial component hierarchy (Phase 1). Nested tree: system > assembly > subassembly > component. 'status' is the verification status of the component's EXISTENCE and placement on the target tractor, not of any part number. Omitted status = unverified. 'appliesTo' uses variant axes from data/configurations.json; omitted = all target configurations. 'supplierClaimedOem' lists OEM numbers quoted by suppliers; they are NOT verified OEM part numbers until checked against parts book SRC-032. IDs are stable and must never be renamed once 3D objects reference them. 'replacementReferences' lists current AGCO supply numbers (SRC-038, 2008 Heritage catalogue) for the part: they are replacement references, not the original 1958 parts-book number. 'confidence' is 'listed' when the catalogue row names the 23C / 35 diesel / FE35 or the 35 without an engine restriction, and 'possible' when the row depends on a US serial range or does not name the engine. Phase 5 fields: 'description', 'function', 'location' and 'failure' (what happens when it fails) are plain-English explanations written from the workshop manual (SRC-035) and general knowledge of the Ferguson System; they describe the part, not a verified part number, and do not change 'status'. 'related' lists hierarchy ids of connected parts for cross-reference chips. Measured values go only in 'specifications' and only with a cited source.

root.name: 1958 Massey Ferguson 35 Diesel
root.description: 1958 Coventry-built Massey Ferguson 35 with the Standard 23C diesel, rear hydraulic lift, three-point linkage and PTO.
root.function: A light general-purpose tractor built around the Ferguson System of implement control.
root.location: The whole machine. Select a system in the left panel or click the model to go deeper.

children.name: Engine: Standard 23C diesel
children.description: Standard Motor Company 23C four-cylinder, four-stroke diesel of 2,259 cc with indirect injection into Ricardo Comet pre-combustion chambers.
children.function: Burns diesel fuel to turn the crankshaft, driving the clutch, gearbox, hydraulic pump and PTO.
children.location: Under the bonnet, bolted at its rear face to the clutch housing. The sump's forward extension carries the front axle.
children.failure: Loss of compression, oil pressure or cooling stops the tractor and can wreck the bearings, liners and head.

specifications.Power: 37.25 bhp bare engine; 34 hp at the PTO

children.name: Cylinder block assembly

replacementReferences.models: Printed "175 23C Diesel Engine"; "175" is almost certainly a misprint for 35

children.description: The cast-iron cylinder block with its four removable wet liners, core plugs, studs and dowels.
children.function: Carries the crankshaft, camshaft and liners and forms the water jacket around the cylinders.
children.location: The main casting of the engine between the sump and the cylinder head.
children.failure: A cracked block or corroded core plug lets coolant into the oil or out onto the ground; frost damage is the usual cause.

children.name: Cylinder block
children.description: Cast-iron cylinder block, open-decked for four wet liners, with bearing webs for the three-bearing crankshaft and the chain-driven camshaft tunnel on the left.
children.function: Holds every rotating part of the engine in line and carries the coolant around the liners.
children.location: Between the sump below and the cylinder head above; the clutch housing bolts to its rear face.
children.failure: Frost cracks and worn liner seats cause coolant loss or oil contamination; a stripped stud thread needs a repair insert.

children.name: Cylinder liner
children.description: Removable cast-iron wet liner (the manual calls it a sleeve) with a top flange seated in a recess in the block and a spigot sealed in the lower block.
children.function: Provides the hard, replaceable bore the piston runs in and passes heat to the surrounding coolant.
children.location: One per cylinder, pressed into the block from the top; the flange stands .001 to .004 in proud of the deck.
children.failure: Wear or scoring lets oil burn and compression drop; a leaking bottom seal puts coolant in the sump. Replaced as a standard-size set with matched pistons, never rebored.

specifications.Grades: F, G, H, matched to pistons

children.notes: Removable flanged sleeves: top flange sits in a recess in the upper block, spigot in the lower block; withdrawn upwards with the pistons (SRC-035 B.32–B.33). The manual does not say wet or dry: SRC-008/SRC-018 say dry, SRC-007 groups the 23C with wet-liner engines. Recorded conflict.

children.name: Core (frost) plugs
children.description: Pressed-steel cup plugs closing the sand-core openings in the block and head water jackets.
children.function: Seal the holes left by casting, and give a weak point that may push out rather than crack the block if the coolant freezes.
children.location: Along the left and right sides of the block and at the ends of the head.
children.failure: Rust through and weep coolant, usually seen as a damp patch and a falling radiator level.

children.name: Block studs and dowels
children.description: Head studs, clutch-housing dowels and the dowel pins that locate the covers on the block.
children.function: Locate the head, timing cover and clutch housing exactly and carry their clamping loads.
children.location: Screwed into the block deck and faces.
children.failure: A stretched or corroded stud will not hold head torque and the gasket blows.

children.name: Cylinder head assembly

replacementReferences.models: 35 and 35X (Eff. Eng. SN SJ41890E), TO35, 23C diesel

children.description: The cast-iron cylinder head with its gasket, studs, Ricardo Comet pre-combustion chambers and the complete valve train.
children.function: Closes the cylinders, carries the valves, injectors and heater plugs, and routes the inlet and exhaust gases.
children.location: Bolted to the top of the block on the head gasket.
children.failure: A blown gasket or cracked head gives white exhaust smoke, coolant loss and bubbles in the radiator.

children.name: Cylinder head
children.description: One-piece cast-iron head with inlet and exhaust ports on the right-hand side, injector and heater-plug bosses on the left, and exhaust valve seat inserts.
children.function: Forms the top of each combustion space and carries the valves, rockers, injectors and heater plugs.
children.location: On top of the block, held down by studs and nuts tightened in sequence.
children.failure: Cracks between valve seats or a warped face let coolant into the cylinders; skimming or replacement is the cure.

children.name: Cylinder head gasket
children.description: Composite or copper-faced gasket with fire rings around the four bores and holes for the water and oil passages.
children.function: Seals combustion pressure, coolant and oil between the head and the block.
children.location: Between the head and the block deck, over the liner flanges.
children.failure: Blows between cylinders or into the water jacket: loss of power, bubbling radiator, milky oil.
children.notes: Copper gasket per SRC-019 top set.

children.name: Head studs / bolts and nuts
children.description: The long studs in the block and the nuts and washers that clamp the head.
children.function: Hold the head down against combustion pressure with the gasket evenly compressed.
children.location: In two rows along the head, tightened from the centre outwards.
children.failure: Under-torqued nuts let the gasket blow; over-torqued studs stretch or pull their threads.
children.notes: Thread form must not be assumed; see SRC-021. Torque per SRC-035 B.29.

children.name: Ricardo Comet pre-combustion chamber
children.description: Ricardo Comet pre-combustion chamber: a heat-resisting insert pressed into the head over each cylinder, with a throat into the main chamber.
children.function: Fuel is injected into this hot, swirling chamber and the burning charge blows into the cylinder, giving smooth indirect-injection combustion.
children.location: One in the underside of the head above each piston, next to the injector and heater plug.
children.failure: A cracked or burnt insert causes knock, smoke and hard starting.
children.notes: Separate insert fitted in the cylinder head (SRC-035 B.38, C section: indirect injection with Ricardo Comet chambers).

children.name: Valve train
children.description: Overhead valves worked by pushrods and rockers from the chain-driven camshaft in the block.
children.function: Opens the inlet and exhaust valves at the right moments in the four-stroke cycle.
children.location: Valves and rockers in the head under the rocker cover; tappets and the camshaft in the block.
children.failure: Wrong clearances make the engine noisy or burn the exhaust valves; a broken spring drops a valve into the cylinder.

specifications.Tip clearance, cold: Inlet .012 in (.305 mm), exhaust .008 in (.203 mm)
specifications.Timing (.015 in checking clearance): IO 10 1/2 deg BTDC, IC 37 1/2 deg ABDC, EO 45 1/2 deg BBDC, EC 10 1/2 deg ATDC

children.name: Inlet valve
children.description: Poppet valve with a larger head than the exhaust valve, seated at 45 degrees in the head.
children.function: Opens on the induction stroke to admit air to the cylinder.
children.location: One per cylinder in the head, stems upward to the rocker.
children.failure: A bent or burnt valve loses compression; a worn stem lets oil down the guide.

children.name: Exhaust valve
children.description: Heat-resisting poppet valve seating on a renewable seat insert in the head.
children.function: Opens on the exhaust stroke to let the burnt gas out to the manifold.
children.location: One per cylinder beside the inlet valve, over the exhaust port.
children.failure: Burns or pits when the clearance closes up, giving misfire and loss of compression.

children.name: Inlet valve guide
children.description: Cast-iron sleeve pressed into the head for the inlet valve stem.
children.function: Keeps the valve square to its seat and controls the oil reaching the stem.
children.location: In the head, one above each inlet port.
children.failure: Wear lets the valve rock and oil pass, with blue smoke and poor seating.

children.name: Exhaust valve guide
children.description: Cast-iron sleeve pressed into the head for the exhaust valve stem.
children.function: Guides the hot exhaust valve and carries heat from its stem into the head.
children.location: In the head, one above each exhaust port.
children.failure: Wear or carbon build-up makes the valve stick open and burn.

children.name: Valve spring, inner
children.description: The smaller of the two concentric coil springs on each valve.
children.function: Adds closing force and damps surge in the outer spring.
children.location: Inside the outer spring, between the head and the spring cap.
children.failure: A broken inner spring lets the valve float at speed; both springs are renewed together.

children.name: Valve spring, outer
children.description: The main coil spring closing each valve.
children.function: Returns the valve to its seat after the rocker opens it and keeps the tappet on the cam.
children.location: Around the valve stem between the head and the spring cap.
children.failure: Weak or broken springs cause valve bounce, noise and burnt seats.

children.name: Valve spring caps and collets
children.description: The spring cap on top of each valve and the pair of split collets that lock it in the stem groove.
children.function: Transfer the spring load to the valve stem.
children.location: At the top of each valve under the rocker.
children.failure: A dropped collet releases the valve into the cylinder with serious damage.

children.name: Rocker shaft
children.description: Hollow steel shaft on pedestals along the head, fed with oil from the block.
children.function: Carries the eight rocker arms and feeds oil to them.
children.location: On top of the head under the rocker cover.
children.failure: Wear or a blocked oilway makes the rockers rattle and seize.

children.name: Rocker arm
children.description: Forged lever pivoting on the rocker shaft, with an adjusting screw and locknut at the pushrod end.
children.function: Turns the upward push of the pushrod into a downward push on the valve, and sets the tappet clearance.
children.location: Eight along the rocker shaft, one over each valve.
children.failure: A worn tip or loose adjuster closes or opens the clearance and the valve burns or clatters.

children.name: Pushrod
children.description: Hollow steel rod with hardened ball and cup ends.
children.function: Carries the cam lift from the tappet in the block up to the rocker.
children.location: Eight along the left side of the engine, running up through the block and head.
children.failure: Bends if a valve sticks, which closes the clearance and holds the valve off its seat.

children.name: Tappet (cam follower)
children.description: Barrel-shaped cam follower sliding in a bore in the block.
children.function: Rides on the camshaft lobe and lifts the pushrod.
children.location: In the block above the camshaft, one per valve.
children.failure: Pitting of the foot wears the cam lobe quickly and makes the engine noisy.

children.name: Rocker cover and gasket
children.description: Pressed or cast cover over the rocker gear with the oil filler cap, sealed by a cork gasket.
children.function: Keeps oil in and dirt out of the valve gear.
children.location: On top of the cylinder head.
children.failure: A hardened gasket weeps oil down the head and onto the manifolds.

children.name: Crankshaft, pistons and connecting rods
children.description: The crankshaft, its main bearings and thrust washers, and the four pistons with their rings, gudgeon pins and connecting rods.
children.function: Turns the push of combustion on each piston into rotation at the flywheel.
children.location: In the lower block and sump, with the pistons running in the liners above.
children.failure: Low oil pressure or dirty oil wears the bearings first; a seized piston or broken rod ends the engine.

children.name: Crankshaft
children.description: Forged steel three-bearing crankshaft with four crankpins, the front end carrying the timing sprocket and pulley, the rear the flywheel.
children.function: Converts the reciprocating motion of the pistons into the rotation that drives everything else.
children.location: Along the bottom of the block in the main bearings.
children.failure: Scored journals from bearing failure; it can be reground to undersize bearings.

children.name: Main bearing shells
children.description: Steel-backed white-metal or copper-lead half shells in the three main bearing housings.
children.function: Support the crankshaft on a film of pressure-fed oil.
children.location: Front, centre and rear of the block, each with a bolted cap.
children.failure: Run when oil pressure or supply fails, with a heavy knock and falling pressure.
children.notes: Std and .010-.040 undersizes listed by SRC-008.

children.name: Crankshaft thrust washers
children.description: Half-ring bearing washers either side of the centre main bearing.
children.function: Take the end thrust of the crankshaft, chiefly from the clutch when the pedal is pressed.
children.location: At the centre main bearing.
children.failure: Worn washers let the crank move fore and aft, felt as a clonk on the clutch pedal.

children.name: Piston

replacementReferences.models: Standard Motor Diesel 23C, MF35X (TO35 column: na)

children.description: Aluminium alloy piston with a recessed crown and four or five ring grooves, graded F, G or H to match its liner.
children.function: Takes the combustion pressure and passes it to the connecting rod.
children.location: One in each liner; numbers 1 and 4 at top dead centre together.
children.failure: Seizure from overheating or scuffing; worn skirts slap when cold.

specifications.Grades: F, G, H matched to the liner

children.notes: 4-ring and 5-ring versions exist (SRC-008): variant/supersession to resolve. Made by Automotive Engineering or Wellworthy (alternatives); graded F/G/H to match the liners; standard size only (SRC-035 B.33).

children.name: Piston ring set
children.description: Cast-iron compression rings and a slotted oil-control ring in the piston grooves (4-ring and 5-ring pistons both exist).
children.function: Seal the piston to the liner and scrape surplus oil back to the sump.
children.location: In the grooves around the top of each piston.
children.failure: Worn or stuck rings give low compression, blow-by from the breather and blue smoke.

children.name: Gudgeon pin and circlips
children.description: Hardened hollow steel pin, fully floating, held by a circlip at each end.
children.function: Joins the piston to the connecting rod and lets the rod swing.
children.location: Through the piston bosses and the small end of the rod.
children.failure: Wear gives a light double knock; a lost circlip scores the liner.

children.name: Connecting rod
children.description: Forged steel H-section connecting rod with a bronze-bushed small end and a split big end on two bolts.
children.function: Links the piston to the crankpin and carries the full combustion load.
children.location: One per cylinder between the piston and the crankshaft.
children.failure: Bends after hydraulic lock, or breaks after big-end failure.

children.name: Small-end bush
children.description: Phosphor-bronze bush pressed into the small end of the rod and reamed to the gudgeon pin.
children.function: Bearing surface for the gudgeon pin.
children.location: In the small end of each connecting rod.
children.failure: Wear produces a sharp knock most noticeable at light load.

children.name: Big-end bearing shells

replacementReferences.models: 23C Diesel, Standard Motors Diesel: 35, 35X, TO35 (undersizes not available)

children.description: Steel-backed half shells in the split big end of each rod.
children.function: Let the rod turn on the crankpin on a film of oil.
children.location: Between the rod, its cap and the crankpin.
children.failure: The first bearing to fail on low oil pressure: a heavy knock that rises with load.

children.name: Connecting rod bolts/nuts
children.description: High-tensile bolts and nuts clamping the big-end cap to the rod.
children.function: Hold the big end together under the inertia loads of the piston.
children.location: Two per rod.
children.failure: A stretched or loose bolt releases the cap and destroys the engine. Fit new nuts on reassembly.

children.name: Crankshaft front oil seal
children.description: Oil seal in the timing cover around the crankshaft nose behind the pulley.
children.function: Keeps timing-case oil off the pulley and belt.
children.location: In the front of the timing cover.
children.failure: Leaks oil down the front of the sump and onto the fan belt.

children.name: Crankshaft rear oil seal
children.description: Rear main seal (rope packing or lip seal) around the crankshaft flange behind the flywheel.
children.function: Stops sump oil reaching the flywheel and clutch.
children.location: At the rear main bearing, inside the clutch housing.
children.failure: Oil on the clutch plate makes it slip and judder; replacing it means splitting the tractor.

children.name: Crankshaft pulley
children.description: V-belt pulley on the crankshaft nose, also used to turn the engine by hand.
children.function: Drives the fan belt, and through it the water pump, fan and dynamo.
children.location: At the very front of the engine behind the radiator.
children.failure: A worn groove throws or chews the belt.

children.name: Camshaft and timing drive
children.description: The camshaft, its bearings and the chain drive from the crankshaft, with the tensioner, sprockets, timing cover and the injection-pump drive.
children.function: Turns the camshaft at half engine speed in step with the crankshaft so the valves and injection are correctly timed.
children.location: At the front of the engine behind the timing cover, with the camshaft running back along the left of the block.
children.failure: A stretched chain retards the valve and pump timing: harder starting, smoke and lost power.
children.notes: SRC-008 lists a 62-pitch timing chain, tensioner and sprockets: camshaft appears chain-driven, not gear-driven as assumed in the product spec. Injection pump drive arrangement still to be established.

children.name: Camshaft
children.description: Forged camshaft with eight lobes, a skew gear for the oil pump and an eccentric at the rear for the fuel lift pump, chain-driven at half crankshaft speed.
children.function: Opens the valves through the tappets and pushrods and drives the oil and fuel lift pumps.
children.location: In the left-hand side of the block, running in three bearings.
children.failure: Worn lobes reduce valve lift and power; a worn skew gear starves the oil pump.
children.notes: Chain-driven (SRC-035, SRC-008). Its rear eccentric drives the fuel lift pump.

children.name: Camshaft bearings
children.description: Three bearings for the camshaft in the block (the manual treats them as bored block bearings or bushes).
children.function: Support the camshaft and meter oil along it.
children.location: Front, centre and rear of the camshaft tunnel.
children.failure: Wear drops oil pressure and lets the chain run slack.

children.name: Timing chain (62 pitches)
children.description: Roller chain of 62 pitches linking the crankshaft and camshaft sprockets.
children.function: Drives the camshaft at half crankshaft speed with the valve timing fixed by the sprocket marks.
children.location: Inside the timing cover at the front of the engine.
children.failure: Stretch and wear retard the timing and make a rattle at idle; a broken chain stops the valves and can bend them.

children.name: Timing chain tensioner
children.description: Spring-loaded rubbing pad (or ratchet tensioner) bearing on the slack run of the chain.
children.function: Takes up chain stretch and stops the chain whipping.
children.location: Inside the timing cover on the slack side of the chain.
children.failure: A worn pad lets the chain slap against the cover.

children.name: Camshaft sprocket
children.description: Sprocket with twice the teeth of the crankshaft sprocket, keyed and bolted to the camshaft nose, carrying the timing mark.
children.function: Drives the camshaft from the chain at half engine speed.
children.location: On the front of the camshaft inside the timing cover.
children.failure: Hooked teeth wear the chain quickly; both are renewed together.

children.name: Crankshaft sprocket
children.description: Small keyed sprocket on the crankshaft nose carrying the other timing mark.
children.function: Drives the timing chain.
children.location: On the crankshaft behind the pulley, inside the timing cover.
children.failure: Worn teeth or a sheared key throw the timing out.

children.name: Injection pump drive
children.description: Gear and shaft taking drive from the timing gear train to the DPA pump, with the pump timed by its slotted mounting flange.
children.function: Turns the injection pump at half engine speed, in step with the crankshaft.
children.location: On the left side of the timing case, behind the injection pump.
children.failure: A sheared key or slipped flange puts the injection timing out: smoke, knock and no start.

specifications.Pump timing: 19 deg BTDC (DPA 3240011/12/13/15); 13 deg BTDC for the light-load-advance pumps; flywheel timing hole locates 16 deg BTDC

children.name: Timing cover and gasket
children.description: Cast cover over the chain and sprockets, carrying the front crankshaft seal and the water-pump mounting, sealed with a gasket.
children.function: Encloses the timing drive and keeps its oil in.
children.location: Front face of the engine behind the pulley.
children.failure: Leaks at the gasket or seal; cracks if the fan hits it.

children.name: Lubrication system
children.description: Rotor oil pump in the sump, full-flow filter, pressure relief valve, oil galleries and pipes, dipstick and breather.
children.function: Keeps every bearing and the valve gear supplied with clean oil under pressure.
children.location: Pump in the sump; filter on the left of the block; galleries cast in the block.
children.failure: Loss of pressure destroys the bearings within minutes.

children.name: Sump (oil pan) and gasket
children.description: Cast oil pan with a forward extension that carries the front axle pivot, sealed to the block by a gasket and drained by a plug.
children.function: Holds the engine oil and, through its forward extension, the front axle.
children.location: Bolted under the block; the front axle pivots in its nose.
children.failure: Leaks at the gasket; a loose drain plug empties the engine.

children.name: Oil pump (rotor type)
children.description: Rotor-type pump driven at engine speed by a skew gear from the camshaft, with a strainer on its pick-up.
children.function: Draws oil from the sump and delivers it through the filter to the main gallery.
children.location: Inside the sump at the front of the engine, driven from the camshaft.
children.failure: Worn rotors give low pressure when hot; a blocked strainer starves the engine.

specifications.Delivery: About 3.95 gal/min at 50 lb/sq in at 2,000 rpm

children.name: Oil filter and element

replacementReferences.models: FE 35 Diesel; TO35 Standard Motors Diesel

children.description: Full-flow canister filter with a replaceable paper element, held by a centre bolt.
children.function: Removes grit and carbon from the oil before it reaches the bearings.
children.location: On the left side of the block below the injection pump.
children.failure: A blocked element opens the bypass and sends dirty oil round; a weeping seal loses oil.

children.name: Oil pipes
children.description: External and internal pipes and galleries carrying oil from the pump to the filter and from the gallery to the rocker shaft and gauge.
children.function: Distribute pressure oil around the engine.
children.location: Along the left side of the block and up to the head.
children.failure: A fractured pipe or loose union loses oil pressure fast.

children.name: Dipstick
children.description: Marked steel rod in a tube down the side of the block.
children.function: Shows the sump oil level between its marks.
children.location: On the left side of the engine.
children.failure: A wrong-length replacement gives a false reading.

children.name: Breather
children.description: Vent pipe from the crankcase (via the rocker cover or side cover) to atmosphere or the air cleaner.
children.function: Releases blow-by gas so crankcase pressure does not push oil past the seals.
children.location: From the top of the engine down beside the block.
children.failure: Blocked, it pressurises the crankcase and forces oil out of every seal.

children.name: Oil pressure relief valve
children.description: Spring-loaded plunger valve in the oil gallery.
children.function: Limits the oil pressure by returning surplus oil to the sump.
children.location: In the pump or gallery on the side of the block.
children.failure: A stuck-open valve gives low pressure; a weak spring the same.

children.name: Flywheel
children.description: Flywheel, starter ring gear and the bolts fixing it to the crankshaft flange.
children.function: Smooths the power strokes, carries the clutch and takes the starter pinion.
children.location: On the rear of the crankshaft inside the clutch housing.
children.failure: Loose bolts or a damaged ring gear.

children.name: Flywheel
children.description: Heavy cast-iron disc with a machined clutch face, a timing hole and the shrunk-on ring gear.
children.function: Stores energy between power strokes, carries the clutch cover and provides the clutch friction face.
children.location: Bolted to the crankshaft flange at the rear of the engine.
children.failure: A scored or heat-checked face makes the clutch judder; the face can be refaced once.

specifications.Timing hole: Locates the engine at 16 deg BTDC

children.name: Starter ring gear
children.description: Hardened steel ring gear of 113 teeth shrunk onto the flywheel rim.
children.function: Meshes with the starter pinion to turn the engine.
children.location: Around the rim of the flywheel.
children.failure: Teeth chip where the engine habitually stops, so the starter spins without engaging.

children.name: Flywheel bolts
children.description: High-tensile set bolts with lock washers or tab plates fixing the flywheel to the crankshaft flange.
children.function: Hold the flywheel on the crankshaft against the clutch and starter loads.
children.location: In a ring around the crankshaft flange.
children.failure: Loosening lets the flywheel fret and knock; the bolt holes elongate.

children.name: Manifolds and exhaust
children.description: Inlet and exhaust manifolds on the right of the head, the exhaust elbow and the vertical silencer.
children.function: Bring clean air to the ports and carry exhaust up and away from the driver.
children.location: Right-hand side of the engine; the exhaust rises beside the bonnet.
children.failure: Cracked manifolds or blown gaskets are noisy and let hot gas onto the fuel pipes.

children.name: Inlet manifold
children.description: Cast inlet manifold feeding the four inlet ports, with the boss for the Thermostart cold-starting aid.
children.function: Distributes the filtered air from the air cleaner to the cylinders.
children.location: Bolted to the right-hand side of the head above the exhaust manifold.
children.failure: A leaking gasket draws unfiltered air and dust straight into the engine.
children.notes: Boss for factory heater reported (SRC-022).

children.name: Exhaust manifold
children.description: Cast-iron manifold collecting the four exhaust ports into one outlet.
children.function: Carries exhaust gas from the head to the elbow and silencer.
children.location: Right-hand side of the head.
children.failure: Cracks from heat cycling; blown port gaskets blow soot and are loud.

children.name: Exhaust elbow (2-hole) and gasket
children.description: Two-bolt cast elbow turning the manifold outlet upward, with its gasket.
children.function: Connects the manifold to the vertical exhaust pipe.
children.location: At the front end of the exhaust manifold.
children.failure: Studs corrode and the gasket blows.

children.name: Silencer (vertical)
children.description: Vertical silencer with a short tail pipe, clamped to the elbow and rising past the right of the bonnet.
children.function: Quietens the exhaust and discharges it above the driver's head.
children.location: Standing on the exhaust elbow beside the bonnet, ahead of the dash.
children.failure: Rusts through at the bottom; a blocked silencer costs power.

children.name: Diesel fuel system
children.description: Gravity-fed diesel system: tank under the bonnet, tap and sediment bowl, lift pump, filter, CAV DPA injection pump and four Pintaux injectors, with an oil-bath air cleaner for the intake.
children.function: Stores, cleans and meters fuel to the cylinders at the right moment and the right quantity for the load.
children.location: Tank above the engine; pump and filter on the left of the engine; injectors in the head.
children.failure: Air in the fuel, dirt or water in the filter, or worn injectors are the usual causes of poor starting, smoke and misfire.

children.name: Fuel tank, cap and tap
children.description: The fuel tank with its filler cap and shut-off tap.
children.function: Holds the fuel supply and lets it be turned off for servicing.
children.location: On top of the engine under the bonnet.
children.failure: Rust and sediment in the tank block the tap and filter.

children.name: Fuel tank

replacementReferences.models: Pony, Pacer, 50, TE20, TO20, TO30, TO35, 40, 50, 65 and others

children.description: Steel tank of 7 1/2 Imperial gallons mounted above the engine so that fuel flows by gravity to the tap.
children.function: Stores the diesel fuel.
children.location: Under the bonnet on the engine mountings, with the filler at the top.
children.failure: Internal rust from condensation; leaks at seams and the tap boss.

children.name: Fuel tank cap
children.description: Vented screw cap on the tank filler.
children.function: Keeps dirt and water out while letting air in as fuel is used.
children.location: Top of the tank, through the bonnet.
children.failure: A blocked vent starves the engine; a bad seal lets rain in.

children.name: Fuel tap

replacementReferences.models: TE 20, TEA 20, 35, 35X, 65, 135 UK, 165 UK and others

children.description: Shut-off tap at the tank outlet, often combined with the sediment bowl.
children.function: Turns the fuel off for filter changes or storage.
children.location: At the bottom of the tank.
children.failure: Weeps at the gland or blocks with sediment.

children.name: Low-pressure fuel circuit
children.description: The sediment bowl, lift pump, filter and pipes between the tank and the injection pump.
children.function: Deliver clean, air-free fuel to the injection pump at a few pounds pressure.
children.location: Left side of the engine.
children.failure: Any air leak on the suction side makes the engine stall and refuse to start until bled.

children.name: Sediment bowl
children.description: Glass bowl with a gauze below the fuel tap.
children.function: Traps water and heavy dirt before the lift pump, where it can be seen and drained.
children.location: Under the tank outlet.
children.failure: A cracked bowl or perished seal draws air into the system.

children.name: Fuel lift pump

replacementReferences.models: 35 and 35X, Eff. Eng. SN SJ37180E, 23C engine
35 and 35X, prior to Eng. SN SJ37180E, 23C engine

children.description: AC type YD diaphragm pump with a hand priming lever, driven by an eccentric at the rear of the camshaft.
children.function: Lifts fuel from the tank line through the filter to the injection pump at 4 to 7 lb/sq in, and primes the system by hand after a filter change.
children.location: Left side of the block, low down towards the rear.
children.failure: A split diaphragm leaks fuel into the sump or stops delivery.
children.notes: SRC-019 lists two different 'Fuel Pump' items for 23C; identity to confirm.

children.name: Fuel filter(s)

replacementReferences.models: FE 35 Diesel; TO35 Standard Motors Diesel

children.description: Paper-element fuel filter with a bleed screw in its head.
children.function: Removes fine dirt and water before the fuel reaches the injection pump.
children.location: On the left of the engine between the lift pump and the injection pump.
children.failure: A blocked element gives power loss at high speed; a bad seal lets air in.

children.name: Fuel pipes and unions
children.description: Low-pressure steel and flexible pipes with unions and banjo bolts.
children.function: Connect the tank, lift pump, filter, injection pump and leak-off.
children.location: Along the left of the engine.
children.failure: Cracked olives or loose unions draw air and cause stalling.

children.name: Injection equipment
children.description: CAV DPA rotary injection pump with its governor, the four high-pressure pipes, the Pintaux injectors and their seals and leak-off pipes.
children.function: Meters and times the fuel into each pre-combustion chamber.
children.location: Pump on the left of the engine; injectors in the left of the head.
children.failure: Worn pump or injectors give hard starting, smoke and uneven running; work on them is for a specialist.

children.name: CAV DPA distributor injection pump
children.description: CAV DPA distributor-type pump with integral variable-speed mechanical governor, driven from the timing case and timed by its slotted flange.
children.function: Pressurises and distributes fuel to each injector in firing order, and governs engine speed from the throttle lever.
children.location: Left side of the engine, driven from the front timing case.
children.failure: Worn plungers or a sticking governor give uneven speed, smoke and hard starting.
children.notes: CAV DPA distributor pump with integral variable-speed mechanical governor. Pump code decides timing (SRC-035 B.41).

children.name: High-pressure injector pipes
children.description: Four heavy-wall steel pipes of equal length from the pump outlets to the injectors.
children.function: Carry the high-pressure fuel pulses to the injectors.
children.location: Over the left side of the engine from pump to head.
children.failure: Cracks at the olives leak fuel and cause a misfire on that cylinder.

children.name: Injector
children.description: CAV nozzle holder clamped into the head, with the nozzle, spring and leak-off connection; heat-shield type on later engines.
children.function: Atomises fuel into the pre-combustion chamber when the pump pressure lifts the needle.
children.location: One per cylinder in the left side of the head.
children.failure: Dribbling or low opening pressure gives smoke and knock.
children.notes: CAV nozzle holder; type depends on engine number, not tractor serial (SRC-035 B.41).

children.name: Injector nozzle
children.description: CAV Pintaux nozzle (a pintle nozzle with an auxiliary starting hole), the type changing with engine number.
children.function: Forms the fuel spray; the auxiliary hole aims fuel at the hot spot for cold starting.
children.location: In the tip of each injector.
children.failure: A blocked or worn nozzle gives a poor spray, smoke and hard starting.

children.name: Injector seals/washers
children.description: Copper sealing washers and dust seals for each injector.
children.function: Seal combustion pressure around the injector body.
children.location: Under each injector in the head.
children.failure: Blow-by past the seal chuffs and carbons the injector; renew every time an injector is removed.

children.name: Fuel return (leak-off) pipes
children.description: Small-bore pipes joining the injector leak-off connections and returning to the filter or tank.
children.function: Return the small quantity of fuel that lubricates the injector needles.
children.location: Along the top of the injectors.
children.failure: A blocked leak-off raises back-pressure and the injectors misbehave; a split pipe drips fuel.

children.name: Air intake
children.description: Oil-bath air cleaner with its intake pipe and pre-cleaner.
children.function: Supplies clean air to the engine.
children.location: Left side under the bonnet, with the intake rising through the bonnet.
children.failure: A neglected cleaner lets dust in and wears the liners fast.

children.name: Oil-bath air cleaner

replacementReferences.description: Bottom oil cup, 12 in diameter, 3 to 4 in inlet

children.description: AC oil-bath cleaner: a wire-mesh element above an oil bowl holding 3/4 pint.
children.function: Air drawn down over the oil drops its dust there and the mesh catches the rest.
children.location: Left side of the engine under the bonnet, connected to the inlet manifold.
children.failure: Low or dirty oil lets dust through to the engine; too much oil is drawn into the engine.

children.name: Intake pipe and pre-cleaner
children.description: Intake stack and pre-cleaner bowl rising through the bonnet, with the hose to the air cleaner.
children.function: Takes the cleanest air available, above the dust, and spins out the heaviest particles.
children.location: Through the left of the bonnet.
children.failure: Perished hose or a loose clip lets unfiltered air in below the cleaner.

children.name: Cooling system
children.description: Pressurised water cooling with a tube-and-fin radiator, belt-driven pump and fan, and thermostat.
children.function: Keeps the engine at working temperature and carries away the heat of combustion.
children.location: Radiator at the front behind the grille; pump and fan at the front of the engine.
children.failure: Blocked tubes, a slipping belt or a stuck thermostat lead to overheating and head damage.

children.name: Radiator

replacementReferences.models: TO35, 35 (Eff. Tr. SN 204181, a US serial), 202

children.description: Vertical tube-and-fin radiator with top and bottom tanks, mounted on the front of the engine frame behind the grille.
children.function: Cools the water with the air drawn through by the fan.
children.location: At the front of the tractor behind the grille.
children.failure: Blocked tubes or fins and leaking seams cause overheating; drain it against frost.

children.name: Radiator cap
children.description: Pressure cap with spring-loaded valve on the top tank filler.
children.function: Raises the boiling point by holding pressure, and vents excess.
children.location: Top of the radiator under the bonnet.
children.failure: A weak spring lets the coolant boil and blow out.

children.name: Top hose
children.description: Moulded rubber hose from the thermostat housing to the radiator top tank.
children.function: Returns hot water from the head to the radiator.
children.location: Top front of the engine.
children.failure: Perishes and bursts; soft spots and bulges are the warning.

children.name: Bottom hose

replacementReferences.models: TO35; 35, 35X (FE) listed under 87 mm petrol and A3.152 rows, 23C not listed separately

children.description: Rubber hose from the radiator bottom tank to the water pump inlet.
children.function: Feeds cooled water back to the pump.
children.location: Low at the front of the engine.
children.failure: Collapses or perishes; a collapsed hose starves the pump at speed.

children.name: Water pump
children.description: Centrifugal pump bolted to the front of the block, driven by the fan belt, with an impeller, a sealed bearing and a carbon face seal.
children.function: Circulates the coolant through the block, head and radiator.
children.location: Front of the engine behind the fan.
children.failure: The seal weeps from the tell-tale hole; worn bearings let the fan wobble.

specifications.Torque: 22–24 lb ft (pump), 26–28 lb ft (pump to block)

children.name: Water pump pulley
children.description: V-pulley on the water pump shaft, carrying the fan.
children.function: Driven by the fan belt, turning the pump and fan together.
children.location: Front of the water pump.
children.failure: A worn groove slips and glazes the belt.

children.name: Fan
children.description: Steel bladed fan bolted to the pump pulley.
children.function: Draws air through the radiator when the tractor is working slowly.
children.location: Between the radiator and the water pump.
children.failure: A cracked blade can go through the radiator.

children.name: Fan belt
children.description: V-belt from the crankshaft pulley driving the water pump and the dynamo, tensioned by swinging the dynamo.
children.function: Drives the fan, pump and dynamo.
children.location: Front of the engine.
children.failure: A slipping or broken belt means overheating and no charge together.

children.name: Thermostat and housing
children.description: Bellows or wax thermostat in a housing on the front of the head, under the top hose.
children.function: Holds coolant in the engine until it is warm, then opens to the radiator.
children.location: In the housing at the top hose outlet.
children.failure: Stuck closed it overheats; stuck open the engine runs cold and sooty.

children.name: Coolant immersion heater
children.description: Electric immersion heater fitted to the block water jacket on cold-climate tractors.
children.function: Warms the coolant before starting in frost.
children.location: Screwed into a core-plug position in the block.
children.failure: Leaks or an open-circuit element.

children.name: Clutch
children.description: Dry plate clutch in the housing between engine and gearbox: a single 10 in disc, or on De Luxe tractors a dual clutch with an 11 in transmission disc and a 9 in disc for the PTO and hydraulic pump.
children.function: Disconnects the engine from the gearbox for gear changes; with the dual clutch the second pedal stage also stops the PTO and pump.
children.location: Inside the clutch housing behind the engine.
children.failure: Slip, judder or drag; a worn dual clutch stops the PTO disengaging at the second stage.

children.name: Clutch (bell) housing
children.description: Cast bell housing bolted between the engine and the gearbox, carrying the release cross-shaft and the starter motor mounting.
children.function: Encloses the clutch and joins the engine to the transmission as a load-bearing part of the tractor's backbone.
children.location: Between the engine and the gearbox, under the dash.
children.failure: Cracks around the mounting faces; blocked drain hole lets oil collect.

children.name: Single-stage clutch assembly
children.description: Single-stage clutch for the standard tractor: 10 in dry driven plate and a cover with 12 green thrust springs.
children.function: Drives the gearbox and, through it, the transmission-driven PTO. The PTO stops whenever the pedal is pressed.
children.location: Bolted to the flywheel.
children.failure: Slip when worn or oiled; judder from a glazed plate.

children.name: Driven plate
children.description: 10 in driven plate with friction linings and a splined hub on the gearbox input shaft.
children.function: Transmits engine torque to the gearbox when clamped against the flywheel.
children.location: Between the flywheel and the pressure plate.
children.failure: Worn linings slip; oil from the rear crank seal makes it judder.

children.name: Pressure plate / cover
children.description: Pressure plate and cover with release levers and 12 thrust springs.
children.function: Clamps the driven plate to the flywheel and releases it when the pedal is pressed.
children.location: Bolted to the flywheel over the driven plate.
children.failure: Weak springs slip; unequal lever heights make it drag.

children.name: Dual-stage clutch assembly
children.description: Dual-stage clutch for the De Luxe tractor: two discs in tandem, an 11 in transmission disc and a 9 in PTO disc, released in turn by one pedal.
children.function: Half pedal travel frees the gearbox for gear changes while the PTO and hydraulics keep running; full travel stops them too. This matches the behaviour the owner reports.
children.location: Bolted to the flywheel.
children.failure: Wear alters the stage points so the PTO will not stop or the gears crunch; adjusting screw clearance is .088 to .092 in.
children.notes: Two discs in tandem: front for the gearbox, rear for the hydraulic pump and PTO. SRC-035 covers the Belleville-spring dual clutch; SRC-015 says an earlier dual clutch is not in manual 1448811M1, so which design a 1958 tractor has is still to check.

children.name: Transmission driven plate
children.description: 11 in driven plate splined to the gearbox input shaft.
children.function: Drives the gearbox; released by the first stage of pedal travel.
children.location: Front disc, against the flywheel.
children.failure: Slip or judder in the drive to the wheels only.

children.name: PTO driven plate
children.description: 9 in driven plate splined to the tubular PTO drive shaft.
children.function: Drives the hydraulic pump and PTO; released only at full pedal travel.
children.location: Rear disc, between the two pressure plates.
children.failure: Slip stops the PTO and hydraulics under load while the tractor still drives.

children.name: Dual clutch cover and pressure plates
children.description: Cover with two pressure plates, two Belleville thrust springs and the release levers with their adjusting screws.
children.function: Clamps both discs and releases them in sequence as the pedal moves.
children.location: Bolted to the flywheel over both discs.
children.failure: Wrong adjustment or worn levers change the stage points.

children.name: Release bearing and carrier
children.description: Graphite or ball thrust bearing on a carrier sliding on the input shaft sleeve.
children.function: Pushes the release levers while the engine turns and the pedal is still.
children.location: In the clutch housing between the fork and the clutch cover.
children.failure: Squeals or rumbles with the pedal pressed; a collapsed bearing stops the clutch releasing.

children.name: Release fork and cross-shaft
children.description: Fork on a cross-shaft through the clutch housing, with the external lever for the pedal rod.
children.function: Moves the release bearing when the pedal is pressed.
children.location: Across the clutch housing.
children.failure: Worn cross-shaft bushes give a stiff, notchy pedal and lost travel.

children.name: Clutch pedal and linkage
children.description: Left-hand pedal with its return spring and the adjustable rod to the release lever.
children.function: Lets the driver release the clutch; free play is set here.
children.location: Left footplate.
children.failure: No free play keeps the release bearing loaded and the clutch slips; too much and it drags.

specifications.Free movement: 3/4 in (19 mm) single clutch; 3/8 in (9.5 mm) dual clutch

children.name: Gearbox
children.description: Three-speed sliding-gear main box with a high/low range gearbox behind it, giving six forward and two reverse speeds, with a 6.6 gallon oil fill shared with the centre housing.
children.function: Gives the driver six forward speeds and two reverse, and carries the PTO drive line through to the rear.
children.location: Between the clutch housing and the centre housing, under the driver's knees.
children.failure: Jumping out of gear, worn bearings and leaking seals.
children.notes: 6 forward / 2 reverse, 3-speed main box with high/low range. Same transmission case for single- and dual-clutch tractors (SRC-035 I.1).

children.name: Gearbox casing (gear pattern cast in)
children.description: Cast-iron casing with the gear pattern cast into its top face, forming part of the tractor's backbone.
children.function: Carries the shafts and bearings and holds the oil.
children.location: Between the clutch housing and the centre housing.
children.failure: Cracks at the flanges if the tractor is split carelessly.

children.name: Input (primary) shaft
children.description: Primary shaft splined to the clutch driven plate, running into the gearbox on a ball bearing.
children.function: Takes the drive from the clutch into the gearbox.
children.location: Front of the gearbox, inside the clutch housing sleeve.
children.failure: Worn splines wear the clutch hub; a failed front bearing growls with the clutch engaged.

children.name: Main shaft
children.description: Output shaft carrying the sliding gears, in line with the input shaft and driving the range gears.
children.function: Carries the selected gear to the range box and the pinion.
children.location: Centre of the gearbox.
children.failure: Worn splines let the sliding gears jump out of mesh.

children.name: Countershaft (layshaft)
children.description: Layshaft with its cluster gear below the main shaft; hollow on dual-clutch tractors so the PTO drive shaft runs through it.
children.function: Carries the constant-mesh gears that the sliding gears engage.
children.location: Low in the gearbox.
children.failure: Worn bearings give a whine in every gear.
children.notes: Hollow on dual-clutch tractors: the pump/PTO drive shaft runs through it (SRC-035 J.4).

children.name: Gear set

replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X, MF50 and MH50 (Eff. Trans. SN CN13566) and others

children.description: The sliding and constant-mesh gears of the three-speed main box, with reverse idler.
children.function: Give the three main ratios and reverse.
children.location: On the main shaft and countershaft.
children.failure: Chipped teeth from crash changes; worn dogs jump out of gear.

children.name: High/low range gears
children.description: High and low range reduction gears behind the main box, with the sliding coupler.
children.function: Double the main-box ratios to give six forward speeds.
children.location: Rear of the gearbox.
children.failure: Worn coupler teeth let it jump out of range under load.

children.name: Selector forks and rails
children.description: Forks on selector rails with spring-loaded detent balls and an interlock.
children.function: Move the sliding gears and hold them in place.
children.location: Under the gearbox top cover.
children.failure: Worn fork tips or weak detents cause jumping out of gear.

children.name: Main gear lever (1-3, R)

replacementReferences.models: Pony, TO20, TEA20, TO30, 35, 40, 50 and others
TE20, TO20, TO30, TO35, TE35, 35, 40, 50, 65 and others

children.description: Main gear lever on the top cover, moving in the pattern cast into the casing.
children.function: Selects first, second, third and reverse.
children.location: Through the gearbox top cover ahead of the seat.
children.failure: Worn ball and socket makes the gate vague.

children.name: Range lever (high / low / start)
children.description: Smaller lever beside the main lever for high, low and the start position.
children.function: Selects the range; the engine will only start with it in the start (neutral) position.
children.location: Through the gearbox top cover beside the main lever.
children.failure: A worn detent lets it drift out of range.

children.name: Gearbox bearings and bushes
children.description: Ball and roller bearings for the shafts, with bronze bushes for the idlers.
children.function: Support the shafts under gear loads.
children.location: In the gearbox casing walls.
children.failure: Rumble and whine; metal in the drained oil is the warning.

children.name: Gearbox top cover and gasket
children.description: Cover plate carrying the gear levers and the selector mechanism, with its gasket.
children.function: Closes the gearbox and carries the gear levers.
children.location: Top of the gearbox ahead of the seat.
children.failure: Leaking gasket; worn lever sockets.

children.name: Rear axle, differential and brakes
children.description: Centre housing with spiral-bevel differential, two axle trumpets, half shafts, hubs and drum brakes.
children.function: Carries the drive from the gearbox to the rear wheels and stops the tractor.
children.location: Rear of the tractor under the seat and mudguards.
children.failure: Leaking axle seals that soak the brakes are the common fault.

children.name: Centre (differential/hydraulic) housing

replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X, MF50, MH50, 65, TO30, TO35 and others
MH50, TO20, TE20, TEA20, TO30, TO35, TE35, 40, 50, 65 and others

children.description: Large cast-iron housing joining gearbox and trumpets, holding the differential, the hydraulic pump and the PTO gears in a shared oil bath, closed on top by the lift cover.
children.function: The rear section of the tractor's backbone and the oil reservoir for the hydraulics.
children.location: Between the gearbox and the axle trumpets.
children.failure: Cracked trumpet flanges from overloading; casting date code on its right side helps date the tractor.
children.notes: Casting date code on RH side forward of round port (SRC-003).

children.name: Differential

replacementReferences.description: Crown wheel and pinion, matched set, light duty
replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X, MF50, MH50, TO35 (Eff. SN 169467) and others

children.description: Spiral-bevel crown wheel and pinion with a four-gear differential in a cage on taper roller bearings.
children.function: Turns the drive through 90 degrees, reduces its speed and lets the wheels turn at different speeds in a turn.
children.location: Inside the centre housing.
children.failure: Whine under load from worn gears or wrong mesh; a broken planet gear locks the axle.

children.name: Crown wheel
children.description: Large spiral-bevel ring gear bolted to the differential cage.
children.function: Driven by the pinion, it gives the final reduction to the axle.
children.location: On the differential cage in the centre housing.
children.failure: Pitting or chipped teeth; renewed only as a matched pair with the pinion.

children.name: Drive pinion

replacementReferences.description: Differential pinion nut, 1-3/4 in NF tapered

children.description: Spiral-bevel drive pinion on the rear of the gearbox output, running in taper roller bearings.
children.function: Drives the crown wheel.
children.location: Between the range gears and the differential.
children.failure: Wrong bearing preload or shimming gives whine and rapid wear.

children.name: Differential cage
children.description: Cast carrier bolted to the crown wheel, holding the cross pin and gears.
children.function: Carries the differential gears round with the crown wheel.
children.location: In the centre housing on the differential bearings.
children.failure: Worn cross-pin holes rattle.

children.name: Differential side and planet gears
children.description: Two side gears splined to the half shafts and two planet gears on the cross pin, with thrust washers.
children.function: Share the drive between the wheels while letting them turn at different speeds.
children.location: Inside the differential cage.
children.failure: Worn thrust washers clonk when the drive is taken up; one wheel spins in mud (hence the diff lock).

children.name: Differential bearings
children.description: Taper roller bearings supporting the differential cage in the centre housing and trumpets.
children.function: Carry the differential and set the crown wheel's position against the pinion.
children.location: Each side of the differential cage.
children.failure: Roughness or play alters the gear mesh and causes whine.

children.name: Differential lock
children.description: Foot-operated dog clutch locking one half shaft to the differential cage, fitted to some tractors.
children.function: Stops one wheel spinning away the drive on slippery ground.
children.location: Right side of the centre housing with a pedal by the right footplate.
children.failure: Worn dogs will not stay engaged; using it in a turn can break it.

children.name: Axle housing (trumpet), LH
children.description: Tapered cast housing bolted to the left of the centre housing, carrying the half shaft, outer bearing and brake backplate.
children.function: Encloses the half shaft and carries the wheel and brake on the left.
children.location: Left rear, under the mudguard.
children.failure: Cracks at the flange; leaking outer seal.

children.name: Axle housing (trumpet), RH
children.description: Tapered cast housing bolted to the right of the centre housing, carrying the half shaft, outer bearing and brake backplate.
children.function: Encloses the half shaft and carries the wheel and brake on the right.
children.location: Right rear, under the mudguard.
children.failure: Cracks at the flange; leaking outer seal.

children.name: Half shaft

replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X, MF50, MH50, TO30, TO35 and others

children.description: Solid steel shaft splined into the differential side gear at one end and carrying the hub and brake drum at the other.
children.function: Drives the rear wheel.
children.location: Inside each axle trumpet.
children.failure: Twisted or broken splines; a worn outer bearing lets the wheel wobble.

children.name: Rear hub
children.description: Flanged hub keyed or splined on the half shaft end, carrying the wheel studs and the brake drum.
children.function: Joins the wheel to the half shaft.
children.location: Outer end of each trumpet.
children.failure: Loose on its taper it fretts and works loose; elongated stud holes.

children.name: Rear wheel studs
children.description: Studs pressed into the hub flange for the rear wheel nuts.
children.function: Hold the rear wheel centre to the hub.
children.location: In the rear hub flange.
children.failure: Stripped threads from over-tightening or running loose.

children.name: Axle oil seals

replacementReferences.description: Rear axle seal, 2-3/4 x 3-5/8 x 19/32 in
replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X, MH50, MF50, TO20, TO30, TO35 and others

replacementReferences.description: Rear axle seal, 2-1/8 x 2-7/8 x 1/2 in

children.description: Oil seals at the outer end of each trumpet, behind the hub.
children.function: Keep the transmission oil off the brakes.
children.location: In the outer end of each axle trumpet.
children.failure: Oil on the brake linings: one brake grabs or does nothing.

children.name: Brakes (shoe type)
children.description: Internal-expanding drum brakes on each half shaft, worked by independent pedals that can be latched together, with a parking latch.
children.function: Stop the tractor, and brake one wheel alone for tight turns.
children.location: Inside the rear wheels on the trumpet ends.
children.failure: Oil-soaked or worn linings and seized adjusters; uneven braking pulls the tractor.

specifications.Turning circle: 17 ft 6 in with independent brakes, 19 ft 3 in without

children.name: Brake drum
children.description: Cast drum bolted between the hub and the wheel centre.
children.function: The rotating surface the shoes press against.
children.location: Inside each rear wheel.
children.failure: Scoring, ovality and heat cracks.

children.name: Brake shoes and linings
children.description: Two shoes per side with riveted linings on a backplate fixed to the trumpet.
children.function: Expand against the drum to brake the wheel.
children.location: Inside each brake drum.
children.failure: Worn or oily linings; renew in axle sets.

children.name: Brake shoe springs
children.description: Return springs pulling the shoes off the drum.
children.function: Release the brake when the pedal is let up.
children.location: Between the shoes inside each drum.
children.failure: A stretched or broken spring lets a shoe drag and overheat.

children.name: Brake cam/expander and adjuster
children.description: Expander and adjuster mechanism on the backplate, worked by the brake shaft.
children.function: Pushes the shoes apart, and takes up lining wear at the adjuster.
children.location: On the brake backplate at each wheel.
children.failure: Seizes if not greased; an unadjusted brake has a long pedal.

children.name: Brake pedals (independent L/R)
children.description: Two pedals on the right footplate, one for each rear wheel, with a latch to couple them for road use.
children.function: Brake either wheel alone, or both together when latched.
children.location: Right footplate.
children.failure: Worn pivots and a weak latch give uneven braking.

children.name: Brake rods and linkage
children.description: Rods, clevises and cross shaft from the pedals to the brake expanders.
children.function: Transmit pedal effort to the brakes, with the adjustment that balances the two sides.
children.location: Along the underside of the footplates to the trumpets.
children.failure: Worn clevis pins give lost pedal travel and uneven braking.

children.name: Parking brake latch
children.description: Ratchet latch holding the coupled pedals down.
children.function: Holds the tractor when parked.
children.location: On the brake pedals.
children.failure: Worn ratchet teeth let the pedals release.

children.name: PTO system
children.description: Rear power take-off driven from the clutch through the gearbox to a six-spline shaft at the rear, with a ground-speed setting.
children.function: Supplies engine power to driven implements at 540 rpm.
children.location: Drive line along the bottom of the gearbox and centre housing; output shaft at the rear below the top link.
children.failure: Worn splines, a leaking rear seal, or failure to engage.

specifications.Speed: 540 rpm at 1,500 engine rpm; 720 rpm at 2,000
specifications.Ground speed setting: One shaft revolution per about 20 in (508 mm) of rear wheel travel
specifications.Live drive: Only with the dual clutch (second pedal stage)

children.notes: Confirmed fitted on the owner's tractor. 540 rpm at 1,500 engine rpm. Live with the dual clutch, through the single clutch otherwise.

children.name: PTO drive shaft (through gearbox)
children.description: On dual-clutch tractors a tubular shaft from the rear clutch disc around the gearbox input shaft, geared to a solid shaft that runs through the hollow countershaft and on to the hydraulic pump and PTO.
children.function: Carries engine power past the gearbox to the hydraulic pump and the PTO, independently of the road gears.
children.location: Along the bottom of the gearbox and centre housing.
children.failure: Worn splines or a failed bearing stop both the PTO and the hydraulics.
children.notes: Dual clutch: tubular shaft from the rear disc around the gearbox input shaft, geared to a solid shaft through the hollow countershaft (SRC-035 J.4).

children.name: PTO gears
children.description: Reduction gears at the rear of the centre housing between the drive shaft and the output shaft, including the ground-speed pick-up.
children.function: Reduce engine speed to 540 rpm at the output shaft, or take drive from the wheels for ground speed.
children.location: In the rear of the centre housing.
children.failure: Chipped teeth or worn bearings make a whine under PTO load.

children.name: PTO engagement lever and coupler
children.description: Lever on the left of the seat moving a sliding coupler between engine, neutral and ground-speed drive.
children.function: Engages or disengages the PTO, and selects ground-speed drive.
children.location: Lever beside the seat; coupler inside the rear of the centre housing.
children.failure: Worn coupler dogs jump out of engagement under load.

children.name: PTO output shaft (rear)
children.description: Six-spline output shaft, 1 3/8 in, running in bearings in the PTO housing at the rear of the centre housing.
children.function: The shaft the implement's drive shaft fits over.
children.location: Rear centre of the tractor, below the top link bracket.
children.failure: Twisted or worn splines, or a bent shaft from a mis-aligned implement.

children.name: PTO housing / bearing retainer
children.description: Cast bearing retainer bolted to the rear of the centre housing, carrying the output shaft bearing and seal.
children.function: Supports the output shaft and closes the rear of the centre housing.
children.location: Rear face of the centre housing.
children.failure: A leaking gasket or seal drips transmission oil at the rear.

children.name: PTO bearings
children.description: Ball bearings for the output shaft and PTO drive line.
children.function: Support the shafts under the side load of the implement drive.
children.location: In the PTO housing and the rear of the centre housing.
children.failure: Roughness or play felt at the output shaft; a rumble when driving an implement.

children.name: PTO oil seals
children.description: Oil seal around the output shaft in the PTO housing, with the housing gasket.
children.function: Keep the transmission oil in at the rear of the tractor.
children.location: In the rear of the PTO housing.
children.failure: A worn seal leaves oil on the shaft and the ground behind the tractor.

children.name: PTO shield / cap
children.description: Shield over the output shaft, with a cap for the shaft when not in use.
children.function: Keeps clothing and hands away from the turning shaft and dirt off the splines.
children.location: Above and around the output shaft at the rear.
children.failure: Missing or bent guards are a serious hazard, not a mechanical one.

children.name: Hydraulic lift system
children.description: Ferguson System hydraulic lift: a constant-running piston pump in the transmission oil, a ram cylinder under the lift cover, a rockshaft with two lift arms, and draft and position control worked from a twin-lever quadrant.
children.function: Raises, lowers and automatically controls the depth of implements on the three-point linkage.
children.location: Pump in the centre housing sump; cylinder, rockshaft and controls under the lift cover on top of the centre housing.
children.failure: A tired pump, leaking ram or sticking control valve shows as slow lift, a load that sinks, or lift arms that hunt up and down.

specifications.Drive: From the PTO drive line; with the dual clutch it runs whenever the secondary disc is engaged

children.notes: Confirmed fitted on owner's tractor. Pump is driven with the PTO drive line, so it runs with the second clutch stage engaged on dual-clutch tractors (SRC-001, SRC-010). Draft control and position control both present (SRC-009, SRC-023).

children.name: Hydraulic pump

replacementReferences.description: Pump repair kit (.91 mm piston): cam blocks, valve chambers, pistons, rings, O-rings

children.description: Four-cylinder piston pump in a cast body that floats on bronze bushes in the centre housing, driven by eccentrics on the PTO drive shaft.
children.function: Draws transmission oil through the strainer and pumps it to the lift cylinder when the control valve calls for lift.
children.location: In the bottom of the centre housing between the gearbox and the differential, under the oil.
children.failure: Worn pistons, cam blocks or valves give slow or no lift, usually worse when the oil is hot.
children.notes: Four-cylinder, constant-running, positive-displacement pump in the sump between gearbox and final drive. Body floats on bronze bushes, held by dowel pins through the centre housing (SRC-035 L.5).

children.name: Pump drive shaft (eccentrics)
children.description: The pump drive shaft, splined to the PTO drive line, carrying two eccentrics for the cam blocks.
children.function: Turns the rotation of the PTO drive into the back-and-forth stroke of the piston yokes.
children.location: Through the pump body, in line with the PTO drive shaft.
children.failure: Worn eccentrics shorten the piston stroke and the pump output falls.
children.notes: The manual calls it the pump drive shaft, with eccentrics carrying the cam blocks.

children.name: Pump camshaft bearing
children.description: Bush or needle bearing supporting the pump drive shaft in the pump body.
children.function: Carries the shaft and the side load from the cam blocks.
children.location: In the pump body at the drive shaft.
children.failure: Wear lets the shaft run out of true and knocks the cam blocks.

specifications.Size (supplier listing): 5/8 in ID x 13/16 in OD x 1/2 in

children.notes: 5/8 in ID x 13/16 in OD x 1/2 in (SRC-012).

children.name: Cam blocks, front and rear

replacementReferences.models: Fits most MF style lift pumps, MK I, II, III
Fits most MF style lift pumps, MK I, II, III

children.description: Front and rear cam blocks riding on the eccentrics inside the two piston yokes.
children.function: Transfer the eccentric motion to the yokes that carry the pistons.
children.location: Inside the pump on the drive shaft eccentrics.
children.failure: Score and wear on their faces, giving a knock and lost output.

children.name: Pump pistons

replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X (Eff. SN 65684), MF50, MH50, TO35 (Eff. SN 179304) and others

children.description: Four pistons in two opposed pairs, carried by the yokes and working in bores in the pump body.
children.function: Displace oil from the inlet valves to the outlet gallery on every stroke.
children.location: Two each side of the drive shaft in the pump body.
children.failure: Scored pistons or bores leak oil back and the lift slows or will not hold.
children.notes: 23.1 mm (SRC-012). Four cylinders (SRC-035 L.5), worked by two piston yokes; supplier kits supply 2.

children.name: Pump piston rings
children.description: Sealing rings on the pump pistons.
children.function: Seal each piston in its bore so the stroke moves oil instead of leaking it back.
children.location: In grooves on the pump pistons.
children.failure: Worn rings cut the pump output, especially when hot.

children.name: Valve chamber assembly
children.description: Two opposed valve chambers, each with an inlet and an outlet valve, bolted to the pump body.
children.function: Let oil into the cylinders on the suction stroke and out to the gallery on the delivery stroke.
children.location: Either side of the pump body.
children.failure: A valve held off its seat by dirt lets oil flow back and the pump loses most of its output.
children.notes: Two opposed valve chambers, each with inlet and outlet valves (SRC-035 L.6).

children.name: Control valve
children.description: Spool valve in the pump worked by the internal control linkage, with lift, neutral and lower positions.
children.function: Directs pump oil to the ram to lift, traps it to hold, or opens it back to the sump to lower.
children.location: In the pump body, moved by the vertical control rod from the lift cover.
children.failure: Sticking or wear makes the lift hunt, creep up, or refuse to hold a load.

children.name: Relief / safety valve

replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X, TO35 (Eff. Tractor SN 168853), MF50, MH50 and others

children.description: Spring-loaded safety valve in the pump outlet gallery.
children.function: Limits the system pressure by dumping oil back to the sump if the load is too great or the arms are at the top.
children.location: In the pump outlet gallery.
children.failure: A weak or leaking valve shows as low lift capacity; a blocked one risks bursting pipes.

children.name: Pump strainer / filter
children.description: Gauze strainer on the pump inlet, cleaned at the transmission oil change.
children.function: Keeps swarf and dirt in the transmission oil out of the pump valves.
children.location: On the pump inlet in the bottom of the centre housing.
children.failure: A choked strainer starves the pump: the lift slows and groans.

children.name: Lift cover assembly
children.description: The lift cover casting with the ram cylinder, piston, connecting rod, rockshaft and lift arms built into it.
children.function: Turns pump pressure into movement of the lift arms.
children.location: On top of the centre housing, under and in front of the seat.
children.failure: Leaking rockshaft seals or a scored ram.

children.name: Lift (top) cover
children.description: Large cast-iron top cover for the centre housing, bored for the rockshaft and the ram cylinder mounting.
children.function: Closes the centre housing and carries the whole lift mechanism.
children.location: Bolted to the top of the centre housing.
children.failure: Cracks at the rockshaft bosses from overloading the arms.

children.name: Lift cover gasket
children.description: Gasket between the lift cover and the centre housing.
children.function: Seals the transmission oil in the housing.
children.location: Under the lift cover flange.
children.failure: Weeps oil along the top of the centre housing.

children.name: Lift (ram) cylinder

replacementReferences.models: 35 (Eff. SN 232850, a US serial), 35X, MF50, 65, TO35 (prior to SN 165554)

children.description: Cast ram cylinder of 3 in bore bolted inside the lift cover, fed from the pump by the oil pipe.
children.function: Houses the piston that pushes the rockshaft round.
children.location: Inside the lift cover pointing rearward at the rockshaft arm.
children.failure: Scoring lets oil past the piston so the arms sink under load.

children.name: Lift (ram) piston, 3 in

replacementReferences.models: 35 (Eff. SN 232850, a US serial), 35X, MF50, 65, TO35 (prior to SN 165554)

children.description: 3 in diameter piston with ring grooves, working in the ram cylinder.
children.function: Takes the pump pressure and pushes the connecting rod against the rockshaft arm.
children.location: In the lift cylinder.
children.failure: Wear or scoring lets the load sink when the engine is stopped.
children.notes: 3 in ring set from serial 65685, so applies to all 1958 tractors (SB-001).

children.name: Lift piston rings / seals

replacementReferences.models: 35 (Eff. SN 232850, a US serial), 35X, MF50, 65, TO35 (prior to SN 165554)

children.description: Sealing rings on the ram piston (3 in ring set from serial 65685).
children.function: Seal the piston in the cylinder so pressure lifts rather than leaks.
children.location: In the grooves of the lift piston.
children.failure: Worn rings are the usual reason a raised implement drops over a few minutes.

children.name: Ram connecting rod
children.description: Short rod with a ball end at the piston and a fork or ball at the rockshaft ram arm.
children.function: Pushes the ram arm of the rockshaft round as the piston moves.
children.location: Between the ram piston and the rockshaft inside the lift cover.
children.failure: Worn ends give lost motion and a clonk when lifting starts.

children.name: Rockshaft (cross shaft)
children.description: Heavy cross shaft (the manual calls it the lift shaft) with a central ram arm and splined ends for the lift arms.
children.function: Carries the lift arms and transmits the ram's push to both of them equally.
children.location: Across the rear of the lift cover above the PTO.
children.failure: Twisted splines or worn bushes let the arms droop or seize.

children.name: Rockshaft bushes
children.description: Four bushes in the lift cover bosses for the rockshaft.
children.function: Bearings for the rockshaft.
children.location: In the lift cover at each side of the rockshaft.
children.failure: Wear lets oil out and the shaft rock.

children.name: Rockshaft O-rings / seals
children.description: O-rings or seals where the rockshaft leaves the lift cover.
children.function: Keep transmission oil in at the rockshaft bosses.
children.location: In the outer ends of the lift cover bosses.
children.failure: The most common lift cover leak, seen as oil running down the trumpets.

children.name: Lift arm, LH
children.description: Forged lift arm splined onto the left end of the rockshaft, with a hole at its tip for the lift rod.
children.function: Lifts the left lower link through the left lift rod.
children.location: Left side of the lift cover, outside the mudguard well.
children.failure: Worn splines let the arm shift so the implement runs tilted.

children.name: Lift arm, RH
children.description: Forged lift arm splined onto the right end of the rockshaft.
children.function: Lifts the right lower link through the adjustable right lift rod.
children.location: Right side of the lift cover.
children.failure: Worn splines or a cracked arm from overloading.

children.name: Control mechanism
children.description: The quadrant with its draft and position levers, the control spring and plunger, the rocker and the internal linkage down to the control valve.
children.function: Let the driver set implement depth or height, and feed the draft load back to the valve so the system holds that depth automatically.
children.location: Quadrant on the right of the seat; spring and rocker at the rear of the lift cover; linkage inside.
children.failure: Wear or wrong adjustment gives hunting arms, a lift that creeps or will not lower.

children.name: Control quadrant (twin lever)
children.description: Curved toothed plate beside the seat carrying the draft and position control levers, with a stop that can be set to the chosen depth.
children.function: Gives the driver a repeatable setting for each lever.
children.location: Right of the seat on the lift cover.
children.failure: Worn teeth or a loose friction disc let the lever creep.

children.name: Draft control lever
children.description: The outer (draft control) lever on the quadrant.
children.function: Sets the working depth of a soil-engaging implement; the system then holds that draft load automatically.
children.location: On the quadrant beside the seat.
children.failure: Lost adjustment between lever and linkage means the implement runs too deep or too shallow.

children.name: Position control lever
children.description: The inner (position control) lever on the quadrant.
