children.function: Holds the lift arms at a fixed height regardless of load, for transport and for implements that do not work in the soil.
children.location: On the quadrant beside the seat.
children.failure: Wrong adjustment stops the arms reaching full height or full drop.

children.name: Draft control (main control) spring
children.description: Large coil spring (the main control spring) in a housing at the rear of the lift cover, behind the top link bracket.
children.function: Measures the push or pull in the top link; its movement is fed to the control valve so the implement depth follows the soil load.
children.location: In the rear of the lift cover, under the top link bracket.
children.failure: A broken or wrongly preloaded spring makes the draft control sluggish or over-sensitive.

children.name: Draft control plunger and seat
children.description: Plunger and seat the control spring bears on, linking it to the rocker.
children.function: Transfers the spring deflection to the internal linkage.
children.location: In the spring housing at the rear of the lift cover.
children.failure: Wear adds lost motion and the system responds late.

children.name: Draft control rocker
children.description: Pivoted lever inside the lift cover between the plunger and the control linkage.
children.function: Turns the spring movement into movement of the control valve rod.
children.location: Inside the rear of the lift cover.
children.failure: A worn pivot gives slack in the draft response.

children.name: Top link bracket (rocker)
children.description: Forked bracket pivoted on the rear of the lift cover with holes for the top link pin, bearing on the control spring.
children.function: Carries the top link and passes its load into the control spring.
children.location: Centre rear of the lift cover above the PTO.
children.failure: Elongated pin holes give slop that upsets the draft control.

children.name: Position control cam and linkage
children.description: Cam and follower linkage that senses the rockshaft angle for position control.
children.function: Returns the control valve to neutral when the arms reach the height set by the position lever.
children.location: Inside the lift cover on the rockshaft.
children.failure: Wear lets the arms overshoot or hunt in position control.

children.name: Internal control linkage
children.description: The levers, rods and fork inside the lift cover that join the quadrant levers, control spring and position cam to the pump's control valve.
children.function: Sums the driver's setting and the feedback from the spring or cam into one movement of the valve.
children.location: Inside the lift cover, dropping down to the pump.
children.failure: Any worn pin here adds slack and the lift hunts; adjustment is set with the cover off.

children.name: Three-point linkage
children.description: Category I three-point linkage: two lower links on ball mountings at the base of the centre housing, lift rods to the lift arms, a levelling lever on the right rod, check chains and a top link on the control-spring bracket.
children.function: Carries the implement and feeds its draft load back into the hydraulic control.
children.location: Rear of the tractor below and behind the seat.
children.failure: Worn pins and ball ends let the implement sway; a seized levelling box cannot be adjusted.
children.notes: Category I (SRC-004). Confirmed fitted on owner's tractor. Top link and implement-side pins are removable implement-related items and must be flagged as such.

children.name: Lower link, LH
children.description: Forged lower link with a ball end at the implement and a ball socket at the tractor, hanging from the left lift rod.
children.function: Carries the implement and transmits its pull to the tractor on the left.
children.location: Left rear, from the centre housing base to the implement.
children.failure: Worn or cracked ball ends; a bent link throws the implement out of line.

children.name: Lower link, RH
children.description: Forged lower link with a ball end at the implement and a ball socket at the tractor, hanging from the right, adjustable lift rod.
children.function: Carries the implement and transmits its pull to the tractor on the right.
children.location: Right rear, from the centre housing base to the implement.
children.failure: Worn or cracked ball ends.

children.name: Lift rod, LH (fixed)
children.description: Fixed-length rod from the left lift arm to the left lower link.
children.function: Transfers the lift to the left lower link.
children.location: Left rear, outside the mudguard.
children.failure: Worn pin holes add play.

children.name: Lift rod, RH with levelling box
children.description: Adjustable rod with a screwed levelling box between the right lift arm and lower link.
children.function: Lifts the right lower link and sets the implement level side to side.
children.location: Right rear, outside the mudguard.
children.failure: A seized thread cannot be adjusted.

children.name: Levelling box (crank handle)
children.description: Screwed adjuster with a crank handle (the manual describes it as a levelling lever) in the right lift rod.
children.function: Lengthens or shortens the right lift rod to level the implement.
children.location: In the right lift rod.
children.failure: Rusts solid if not greased.
children.notes: The manual describes a levelling lever on the right-hand lift rod (SRC-035 L.5).

children.name: Top link

replacementReferences.models: 135 UK, 35, 35X, TE20, TEA20, TO20, TO30 and others

children.description: Adjustable screwed link with ball ends between the top link bracket and the implement mast. It is removable and is also supplied with implements.
children.function: Sets the implement pitch and carries the draft load into the control spring.
children.location: Centre rear, above the PTO.
children.failure: Seized thread or worn balls; a wrong length upsets the draft control.

children.name: Check chains / stabilisers

replacementReferences.description: Stabiliser kit, Cat 1 (2 arms, 2 brackets and pins)
replacementReferences.models: TE20, TEA20, TO20, TO30, TO35, 35, 40 Utility, 50 Utility

children.description: Chains from the lower links to the axle housing with adjusters.
children.function: Limit the sideways swing of the implement.
children.location: Either side under the trumpets.
children.failure: Stretched chains let the implement hit the tyres.

children.name: Linkage pins and linch pins
children.description: Pins and linch pins for the lift rods, links and top link.
children.function: Make the connections quick to attach and release.
children.location: At each joint of the linkage.
children.failure: Lost linch pins drop an implement; worn pins add play.

children.name: Lower link ball ends
children.description: Category I ball ends in the lower links, with forward ball mountings at the base of the centre housing.
children.function: Let the links swivel freely on the tractor and the implement.
children.location: Both ends of each lower link.
children.failure: Worn balls give slop in the implement.

children.name: Drawbar

replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X, TO30, TO20, TE20, TEA20, TO35, MF50, MH50 and others

replacementReferences.description: Swinging drawbar kit (drawbar, bracket, clevis pin)

children.description: Swinging drawbar on a frame under the centre housing, or a drawbar carried on the lower links.
children.function: Pulls trailed implements and trailers.
children.location: Under the PTO at the rear.
children.failure: Worn pin holes; overloading bends it.

children.name: Front axle and steering
children.description: Adjustable-track beam axle pivoted in the front of the sump extension, with stub axles on kingpins, radius rods, and a worm-and-nut steering box under the dash.
children.function: Carries the front of the tractor and steers it.
children.location: Under the radiator.
children.failure: Worn kingpin bushes and pivot pin make the steering wander.

children.name: Front axle centre beam
children.description: Centre section of the axle, pivoted at the sump nose, with the telescopic extensions clamped into each end.
children.function: Carries the front weight on the pivot and lets the axle rock over rough ground.
children.location: Under the radiator.
children.failure: Worn pivot bore; cracks at the extension clamps.

children.name: Adjustable axle extensions
children.description: Telescopic outer axle sections with the kingpin housings, bolted at the chosen track width.
children.function: Set the front track between 48 and 80 in.
children.location: Each end of the axle beam.
children.failure: Seized in the beam; worn kingpin bores.

children.name: Axle pivot pin and bush
children.description: Pin and bush at the nose of the sump extension on which the axle rocks.
children.function: Lets the axle oscillate so both front wheels stay on the ground.
children.location: Front of the sump below the radiator.
children.failure: Wear lets the axle clonk and the steering wander.

children.name: Radius rods
children.description: Rods from each axle extension back to a pivot under the clutch housing.
children.function: Brace the axle against fore-and-aft loads while it rocks.
children.location: Each side under the engine.
children.failure: Worn rear ball joints let the axle move backwards under braking.

children.name: Stub axle / spindle
children.description: Spindle with the kingpin forged at right angles to it, running in the extension housing, with the steering arm on top.
children.function: Carries the front hub and turns it for steering.
children.location: Each end of the front axle.
children.failure: Worn kingpin or bent spindle after hitting a kerb.

children.name: Kingpin bushes
children.description: Bronze bushes and thrust washer for each kingpin in the axle extension.
children.function: Let the stub axle turn freely and carry the front weight on the thrust washer.
children.location: In each axle extension housing.
children.failure: Wear gives wheel wobble and a camber change you can see.

children.name: Front hub and bearings

replacementReferences.description: Wheel bearing kit, one wheel (2 cones, 2 cups, 1 seal)

children.description: Hub on two taper roller bearings with an oil seal and a grease cap.
children.function: Carries the front wheel on the stub axle.
children.location: Each front wheel.
children.failure: Rough bearings or wrong end float; repack with grease at service.

children.name: Steering box

replacementReferences.description: Steering shaft bearing kit (2 bearings, 2 cups)

children.description: Steering gear at the base of the column, driving a pair of drop arms to the drag links. It holds 1.8 pints of oil.
children.function: Turns the steering wheel movement into the movement of the drag links.
children.location: Under the dash on top of the clutch housing.
children.failure: Worn gear gives free play at the wheel; leaks at the drop arm seals.

children.name: Steering column
children.description: Tube and shaft from the steering wheel through the dash to the steering box.
children.function: Carries the wheel and connects it to the box.
children.location: Rising from the box through the dashboard.
children.failure: Worn top bush lets the wheel rock.

children.name: Steering wheel

replacementReferences.description: Steering wheel, black ribbed, 17-5/8 in, keyed hub, 11/16 in shaft
replacementReferences.models: TE20, TO20, TO30, TE35, 35, 40, 50, 65 and others

replacementReferences.description: Steering wheel nut, chrome, 13/16 in NF
replacementReferences.models: TE20, TO20, TO30, TE35, 35, 40, 50 and others

children.description: Three-spoke wheel with a moulded rim on a splined column shaft.
children.function: The driver's steering control.
children.location: Top of the steering column.
children.failure: Cracked rim; loose on worn splines.

children.name: Drag links / track rods
children.description: Two rods with ball joints from the steering box drop arms to the steering arms, lengthened to suit the track setting.
children.function: Carry the steering movement to each stub axle.
children.location: Each side under the engine.
children.failure: Worn ball joints give free play and uneven toe.

children.name: Steering arms

replacementReferences.models: TO20, TE20, TO30, TEA20, TO35, 35, 135 UK, 240S Turkey, 240

children.description: Arms clamped on top of each stub axle for the drag link ball joints.
children.function: Turn the stub axles.
children.location: On top of each kingpin.
children.failure: Loose clamp bolts let the arm move on the kingpin and the tracking goes off.

children.name: Electrical system
children.description: 12 volt Lucas system from two 6 volt batteries: dynamo and control box, starter, cold-start aid, lights, horn and instruments.
children.function: Starts the engine, warms the intake for cold starts, and powers lights and instruments.
children.location: Batteries under the bonnet; dynamo and starter on the engine; instruments in the dash.
children.failure: Poor earths and corroded terminals cause most faults; the diesel runs without electricity once started.

specifications.Batteries: 38 Ah at 10 h, 43 Ah at 20 h

children.notes: Lucas equipment (SRC-003). Voltage is a variant axis.

children.name: Starter motor (Lucas M45G)
children.description: Lucas M45G inertia starter with an 11-tooth pinion that engages the 113-tooth flywheel ring.
children.function: Turns the engine over for starting against 20:1 compression.
children.location: On the right of the clutch housing, engaging the flywheel.
children.failure: Worn brushes or a jammed pinion; a slow starter in winter usually means poor connections.

children.name: Dynamo
children.description: Lucas C39P2 two-brush dynamo on a swinging bracket, driven by the fan belt.
children.function: Charges the batteries and supplies the lights with the engine running.
children.location: Right front of the engine, belt-driven from the crankshaft pulley.
children.failure: Worn brushes or bearings; no charge shows on the ammeter.

children.name: Control box (voltage regulator)
children.description: Lucas control box with cut-out and voltage regulator.
children.function: Connects the dynamo to the batteries when it is charging and limits its output.
children.location: Under the bonnet or dash.
children.failure: Burnt points give over- or under-charging; a stuck cut-out flattens the batteries overnight.

children.name: Battery / batteries
children.description: Two 6 volt batteries connected in series for 12 volts, 38 Ah at the 10-hour rate.
children.function: Store electricity for starting and lighting.
children.location: Under the bonnet beside the fuel tank.
children.failure: Sulphated cells or corroded terminals; a diesel needs a full battery to start.
children.notes: Two 6 V batteries in series (12 V), 38/43 Ah (SRC-035 B.42).

children.name: Battery cables

replacementReferences.models: 35 (prior to SN 216684 Deluxe and 220038 Special, US serials), TO35 Deluxe, 85, 88, Super 90

children.description: Heavy cables from the batteries to the starter switch and earth, with the series link.
children.function: Carry the starter current.
children.location: From the battery tray to the starter and the chassis earth.
children.failure: Corroded ends drop volts and the starter turns slowly.

children.name: Starter switch
children.description: Heavy-current switch, worked from the dash or the gear lever safety start, that connects the batteries to the starter.
children.function: Energises the starter only when the range lever is in the start position.
children.location: On the dash or gearbox cover.
children.failure: Burnt contacts give a click and no crank.

children.name: Heater (glow) plugs
children.description: Glow plugs in the pre-combustion chambers on cold-climate tractors.
children.function: Heat the chambers before starting in severe cold.
children.location: In the left side of the head beside the injectors.
children.failure: Burnt-out elements; a shorted plug flattens the battery.

children.name: Cold-start aid (Thermostart / Ki-gass)

replacementReferences.models: 35 Diesel, 50 MF and MH, 65, 85, 88, Super 90, 130 French, 135 UK and others

children.description: CAV Thermostart in the inlet manifold, which heats and ignites a trickle of fuel in the intake air, or alternatively Ki-gass priming equipment.
children.function: Warms the intake air for cold starting.
children.location: Screwed into the inlet manifold, with a small fuel feed and a switch on the dash.
children.failure: A dry fuel feed or a dead element gives long cranking in cold weather.
children.notes: CAV Thermostart fitted to the inlet manifold, or Ki-gass equipment (SRC-035 B.41). Which one is fitted to the owner's tractor is unknown.

children.name: Wiring harness and terminals
children.description: Cloth- or PVC-covered loom with bullet and Lucar terminals linking the control box, switches, lamps and instruments.
children.function: Distributes current around the tractor.
children.location: Along the engine and under the bonnet to the dash.
children.failure: Chafed or perished insulation shorts to earth.

children.name: Headlamps

replacementReferences.models: MH50, TO20, TE20, TEA20, TO30, TO35, 35, 40, 50 and others (US sealed-beam pattern)

children.description: Pair of lamps in pods either side of the grille.
children.function: Road and yard lighting.
children.location: On the front grille shell.
children.failure: Corroded reflectors and poor earths.

children.name: Rear / plough lamp
children.description: Combined rear lamp or a swivelling plough lamp on the mudguard.
children.function: Rear light for the road, or light on the implement at night.
children.location: On a mudguard or the seat bracket.
children.failure: Vibration breaks bulbs and mountings.

children.name: Ammeter
children.description: Centre-zero ammeter in the dash.
children.function: Shows charge or discharge of the batteries.
children.location: In the dashboard.
children.failure: A loose terminal here can stop the whole system since the charge current passes through it.

children.name: Water temperature gauge
children.description: Capillary or electric water temperature gauge in the dash with its sender in the head.
children.function: Shows the coolant temperature.
children.location: Dashboard; sender in the cylinder head.
children.failure: A broken capillary leaves the needle on cold.

children.name: Oil pressure gauge
children.description: Direct-reading pressure gauge in the dash fed by a small pipe from the oil gallery.
children.function: Shows the engine oil pressure, normally 40 to 60 lb/sq in.
children.location: Dashboard, with the pipe along the engine.
children.failure: A fractured pipe pumps oil over the engine; watch this gauge at every start.

children.name: Tractormeter

replacementReferences.models: 35, 35X: 23C Diesel, 87 mm petrol and VO (prior to SN 307657)

children.description: Combined engine rev counter, hour meter and PTO speed indicator, driven by a cable from the engine, fitted to De Luxe tractors.
children.function: Shows engine speed, the 540 rpm PTO mark and hours worked.
children.location: Centre of the dashboard.
children.failure: A broken cable or dry drive.
children.notes: Listed as a De Luxe feature (SRC-010). Fitment depends on the De Luxe package, which is not yet a separate variant axis. Fitted on the De Luxe (dual clutch) version (SRC-035 B.1).

children.name: Horn
children.description: Electric horn with a push on the dash.
children.function: Warning signal.
children.location: Under the bonnet or on the dash.
children.failure: Corroded contacts.

children.name: Bodywork and operator area
children.description: Hinged bonnet, side panels, grille, badges, dashboard, mudguards, seat and footplates, in the grey and red livery.
children.function: Covers the engine and fuel tank, keeps mud off the driver and gives them somewhere to sit and stand.
children.location: Over the engine and around the operator.
children.failure: Rust and dents; the sheet metal carries no mechanical load.

children.name: Bonnet
children.description: One-piece pressed bonnet over the tank and engine, hinged or lifting off, with the air intake and filler through it.
children.function: Covers the fuel tank and engine.
children.location: Top of the tractor between the grille and the dash.
children.failure: Rust along the lower edges; cracks at the hinge.

children.name: Side panels
children.description: Removable pressed panels each side of the engine between bonnet and footplates.
children.function: Close the engine bay.
children.location: Each side of the engine.
children.failure: Dents and rust; often missing on working tractors.

children.name: Grille
children.description: Front grille shell with a mesh insert and the headlamp pods.
children.function: Protects the radiator while letting the air through.
children.location: Front of the tractor.
children.failure: Dents from implements; a blocked mesh overheats the engine.

children.name: Front badge / emblem
children.description: Badge on the grille, either Ferguson or Massey Ferguson depending on the build date during 1958.
children.function: Identifies the maker and helps date the tractor.
children.location: Top of the grille.
children.failure: Often lost or replaced, so not proof of date on its own.
children.notes: Ferguson vs Massey Ferguson branding changed during 1958 (SRC-002). Variant.

children.name: Dashboard / instrument panel
children.description: Pressed instrument panel at the rear of the bonnet carrying the gauges, switches and the steering column.
children.function: Holds the instruments in front of the driver.
children.location: Behind the bonnet above the clutch housing.
children.failure: Cracked around the gauge holes.

children.name: Tractor serial number plate
children.description: Stamped plate riveted to the dash panel carrying the prefix letters and the serial number.
children.function: Identifies the tractor's chassis, engine, clutch type and build sequence.
children.location: On the dash panel below the instruments, left or right side depending on build.
children.failure: Missing or illegible plates make the tractor hard to date; the engine number is then the next clue.

children.name: Rear mudguards (fenders)

replacementReferences.description: Fender skin, less bracket (LH or RH)
replacementReferences.models: TO20, TO30, TO35, TE20, 35, 40, 50, 65 and others

children.description: Pressed steel rear mudguards bolted to the axle trumpets, carrying the rear lamp and often a toolbox.
children.function: Keep mud off the driver and give a handhold.
children.location: Over each rear wheel.
children.failure: Rust at the mounting brackets and cracks from vibration.

children.name: Seat (pan or cushioned De Luxe)

replacementReferences.models: TE20, TEA20, TO20, TO30, TO35, 35, 35X, 50 and others

replacementReferences.description: Seat cushion assembly, grey with red trim

children.description: Pressed pan seat on the standard tractor, or a cushioned seat on the De Luxe.
children.function: The driver's seat.
children.location: Over the lift cover on its spring support.
children.failure: Rusted pan or perished cushion.
children.notes: De Luxe version has a cushion seat (SRC-035 B.1).

children.name: Seat support / spring
children.description: Pivoted bracket and coil spring carrying the seat on the lift cover.
children.function: Cushions the ride.
children.location: Behind the lift cover, over the PTO.
children.failure: A broken spring or worn pivot gives a hard ride.

children.name: Footplates / steps
children.description: Steel platforms each side with steps, carrying the pedals.
children.function: Give the driver a footing and carry the clutch and brake pedals.
children.location: Each side of the gearbox.
children.failure: Cracked around the pedal pivots.

children.name: Front weights (optional)

replacementReferences.models: MH 50; MF50, TE20, TEA20, TO20, TO30, TE35, TO35, 40, 50 and others

children.description: Optional cast weights hung on the front of the axle or a frame.
children.function: Hold the front down with a heavy rear-mounted implement.
children.location: Front of the tractor below the grille.
children.failure: Not a wearing part; the mounting bolts need to be checked.

children.name: Wheels and tyres
children.description: Pressed front wheels and rear wheels with adjustable rims clamped to dished centres, on agricultural tyres.
children.function: Carry the tractor and put the drive into the ground; the rear rims adjust the track.
children.location: Front 4 x 19 and rear 10 x 28 as supplied.
children.failure: Cracked centres around the stud holes and rusted rims.

children.name: Front wheel (disc and rim)

replacementReferences.models: MH 50; MF TE20, TEA20, TO20, TO30, TE 35, TO35, MF35, 40, 50 and others

children.description: One-piece pressed disc and rim for the 4 x 19 tyre.
children.function: Carries the front tyre on the hub.
children.location: Each front hub.
children.failure: Bent rim or elongated stud holes.

children.name: Rear wheel centre (disc)
children.description: Dished steel disc bolted to the rear hub, with lugs for the rim clamps.
children.function: Joins the rim to the hub; reversing the dish is one way of changing the track.
children.location: Each rear hub.
children.failure: Cracks at the stud holes and clamp lugs.

children.name: Rear rim
children.description: Steel rim for the 10 x 28 tyre with lugs for the clamps.
children.function: Carries the rear tyre; its position on the centre sets the track.
children.location: Each rear wheel.
children.failure: Rust at the bead seat lets the tyre lose air.

children.name: Rim clamps / bolts
children.description: Wedge clamps and bolts fixing the rim to the centre lugs.
children.function: Hold the rim at the chosen track position.
children.location: Between the rim lugs and the centre.
children.failure: Loose clamps let the rim shift and shear the bolts.

children.name: Front wheel nuts

replacementReferences.description: Lug bolt, 1/2 in-20 x 1-3/4 in, serrated shoulder
replacementReferences.models: MH 50; MF TE20, TEA20, TO20, TO30, TO35, MF35, 40, 50 and others
TO20, TO30, TO35, TE20, TEA20, 35, 35X and others

children.description: Nuts on the front hub studs.
children.function: Hold the front wheel to the hub.
children.location: Each front wheel.
children.failure: Working loose; check after refitting a wheel.

children.name: Rear wheel nuts

replacementReferences.description: Lug bolt, 9/16 in x 2 in NF

children.description: Large nuts on the rear hub studs.
children.function: Hold the rear wheel centre to the hub.
children.location: Each rear wheel.
children.failure: Working loose; elongated holes in the centre follow.

children.name: Front tyre
children.description: Ribbed steering tyre, 4 x 19 as supplied, at 26 lb/sq in.
children.function: Steers and carries the front of the tractor.
children.location: Each front wheel.
children.failure: Cracked sidewalls from age; under-inflation wears the ribs.
children.notes: Size as supplied; the owner's tyres may differ.

children.name: Rear tyre
children.description: Traction-lug tyre, 10 x 28 as supplied, at 12 lb/sq in, often water-ballasted.
children.function: Puts the drive into the ground.
children.location: Each rear wheel.
children.failure: Worn lugs lose grip; cracked sidewalls.
children.notes: Size as supplied; the owner's tyres may differ.

children.name: Tyre valves
children.description: Inner tube valves, with water-ballast valves on the rear.
children.function: Inflate the tubes and admit ballast.
children.location: Through each rim.
children.failure: Corroded valves leak slowly.
